land.text: Umma, whose ensi Lugal-zage-si 'established his new capital' at Uruk and ruled Sumer from there

successors.note: Not a conquest: Umma's ruler became king of the collective (its -2340 rename event); Umma then 'Under the Akkadian Empire ... was a major power and economic center rivaled only by Adab and Uruk'.

capitals.name: Umma (Tell Jokha)
capitals.note: 'traditionally identified with Tell Jokha', Dhi Qar Province; Umm al-Aqarib has also been suggested. Not in the gazetteer.

correction.text: the city of Umma and its fields toward the Gu-edena, the plain disputed with Lagash ('Best known for its long frontier conflict with Lagash, as reported c. 2400 BC by Entemena')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Umma polity. Lugal-zage-si's conquests (Lagash, Uruk, Ur, Kish, c. 2358–2340) are the collective's rename and its occupation of Ur, not Umma's territory (the first version's ledger gain of Ur and Uruk at -2350 was dropped to agree with this). Under Lagash's tribute -2450..-2425 the city is drawn with the vassal tint (ledger). The radius is this dossier's.

ledger.note: 2500 BCE: Umma a city-state under Kish's arbitration. Mesilim of Kish '(c. 2500 BC)' 'acted as arbitrator in a Lagash–Umma conflict' (the Kish page dates him c. 2550); Ur-Nanshe of Lagash (c. 2520) 'captured the king of Umma, Pabilgaltuk' (History of Sumer page). The founding year is bridged to Mesilim.

region.text: 'the Guʾedena, a fertile area lying between them'

ledger.note: 2450 BCE: war with Lagash over the Gu-edena. 'In c. 2450 BC, Lagash and the neighboring city of Umma fell out with each other after a border dispute over the Guʾedena'; Eannatum defeated Ush and made 'a boundary treaty with Ush's successor, Enakalle' (r. c. 2445); Umma 'a tributary' of Lagash c. 2450–2425 (lagash ledger).

2450 BCE: Umma pays tribute to Lagash. 'Eannatum made Umma a tributary, where every person had to pay a certain amount of grain'; the History of Sumer page: 'Umma became tributary under Eannatum'. Vassal tint on Umma's own city (umma_-2500). Mirror of lagash /ledger/3.

2425 BCE: Umma throws off the tribute. Under Enannatum I (c. 2425) 'Umma once more asserted independence under its ensi Ur-Lumma, who attacked Lagash unsuccessfully'. Year bridged to Enannatum I's accession. Mirror of lagash /ledger/7.

2400 BCE: Entemena of Lagash settles the frontier (the end is bridged: the page dates only Entemena's report, not a settlement; reviewer me-01 lowered confidence from 2). The conflict was 'reported c. 2400 BC by Entemena'; Ur-Lumma (r. c. 2425) and Il (r. c. 2420, 'temp. of Entemena') had renewed it; Giššakidu (r. c. 2400) follows.

2340 BCE: Lugal-zage-si moves his capital to Uruk and rules Sumer. He 'annexed most of the territory of Lagash under king Urukagina', 'invaded Kish, where he overthrew Ur-Zababa, Ur, Nippur, and Larsa' and 'established his new capital' at Uruk: Umma's city-state becomes a city of the collective's last kingdom (rename in sumerian-city-states). Under Akkad Umma had its own governor (Šubur-Nagarpae; Naram-Sin settled an Adab–Umma boundary dispute), under the Gutians governors 'Vassal to the Gutian dynasty', under Ur III a province of four districts (Da-Umma, Apisal, Gu'edena, Mušbiana). [fixer me-01: region trimmed from Umma, Ur and Uruk to Umma alone, and the -2350 gain of Ur and Uruk dropped: the Umma page says only that the city 'reached its zenith c. 2350 BC, under the rule of Lugal-Zage-Si who also controlled Ur and Uruk', a king's conquests, which sumerian-city-states books as its rename (-2340) and its hold on Ur; Umma's own keyframe never drew them.]

wars.name: Lagash–Umma border conflict

zones.text: 'the Guʾedena, a fertile area lying between them'

wars.outcome: Ush defeated by Eannatum (Stele of the Vultures), boundary treaty with Enakalle, Umma tributary; Ur-Lumma and Il fought Entemena, who 'reported' the conflict c. 2400.
wars.note: Gu-edena is not in the gazetteer; it lies between Umma (Tell Jokha, 45.87 E 31.63 N) and Girsu (46.17 E 31.56 N).

wars.name: Lugal-zage-si's conquest of Sumer
wars.outcome: Umma's ensi conquered Lagash, Uruk, Ur, Kish, Nippur and Larsa and ruled Sumer from Uruk until Sargon.

certainty.note: The Gu-edena boundary with Lagash is the one dated line (Mesilim's arbitration, Eannatum's treaty, Entemena's report); the rest is a city territory.

sources.title: Umma
sources.note: Location, rulers with dates (Enakalle c. 2445, Ur-Lumma c. 2425, Il c. 2420, Giššakidu c. 2400, Lugal-zage-si c. 2340), zenith c. 2350, Umma under Akkad, Gutians, Ur III, Sumuel.

sources.title: Lugal-zage-si
sources.note: Ensi of Umma; conquests; capital Uruk.

sources.title: Eannatum
sources.note: Ush defeated; treaty with Enakalle; Umma tributary.

sources.title: History of Sumer
sources.note: Pabilgaltuk captured by Ur-Nanshe; Ur-Lumma's attack; Il subdued by Entemena.

sources.title: Enannatum I
sources.note: Reign c. 2425; Umma under Ur-Lumma asserted independence and attacked Lagash; Il; the page is silent on the end of Lagash's hegemony.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks: the city-state of Umma from Mesilim's arbitration (c. 2500, the first dated mention; the start is bridged) to Lugal-zage-si's move to Uruk (c. 2340), when its ruler's kingdom becomes the collective's last phase. Lugal-zage-si's conquests are recorded as the collective's rename and its hold on Ur (me-01 fix: the gain of Ur and Uruk at the zenith c. 2350 was removed here, because the keyframe never drew them; the Umma page's 'also controlled Ur and Uruk' is kept in the dissolve note). Umma's later life as an Akkadian, Gutian and Ur III province is not a state. The collective sumerian-city-states books the dissolve as a gain (-2340) since the me-01 fix; Umma is Lagash's vassal -2450..-2425 (mirror of lagash). Umma and the Gu-edena are not in the gazetteer.
